output.confusing_rules: The win condition is a little hard to parse: it says factions win by having players alive at the end, but also that the game ends as soon as the living players belong to a single faction, with exceptions for Jesters and Executioners. A concrete example of how Neutral players affect that check would help. It was also unclear whether a role-blocker is told if the target had an action to block.
output.missing_information: I couldn't tell from the night report whether my role-block had actually prevented an action; the target, Alice, was Vanilla, so there may have been nothing to block. More generally, a short private action-resolution report clarifying what succeeded or had no effect would be useful without revealing information the role shouldn't know.
output.bugs_or_oddities: My death announcement included a detailed last will, but I didn't see an explicit opportunity to write or update that will in the conversation. Also, after Night 2 began, the transcript jumps to Ivan's death on Day 3 night without showing the intervening results or Day 3 events. That may be intentional for a dead player's view, but it makes the game record feel incomplete.
output.suggestions: Make will entry an explicit step at the start of each day, and show a clear confirmation when a will is saved. Consider providing dead players with the completed public event log after the game ends. A brief rules example for faction parity and Neutral win checks would also reduce ambiguity.

answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As Dave I wanted to confirm via a private channel with Carol and Ivan what their night actions actually were, and to coordinate framing or a Katana handoff without it being visible. I also wanted to see the moderator's confirmation of whether my Katana attack hit, since the attacked player's reveal was only partial. Nothing else stood out.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Dave's death on Day 2 was attributed to a Vigilante, yet Dave was alive-announced after Night 1 and the Katana attack on Alice was reported as surviving via Medic protection; the Vigilante shot was never explained in the night summary. Erin nominated herself repeatedly and the self-nomination mechanic let a Jester-like player force multiple trials. Ivan's death was announced at 'Day 3 night' rather than as a day event, which was inconsistent with the stated announcement timing. Two Medic claims existed simultaneously with no moderator resolution.
answers.suggestions: Publish a concise night summary listing each action's visible result (attacks, protections, role-blocks, investigations) so players do not need to reconstruct it. Clarify whether self-nominations count toward the three-nomination day limit. Provide a clearer statement of how Katana handoffs and holder status are reported to the Yakuza chat. Allow optional private-channel confirmation of teammate actions. Make the moderator verify Medic claims when two players claim the role, or at least announce the protected target count.

The Katana holder's visibility to Sheriffs versus the Katana attack disguise was hard to parse. answers.bugs_or_oddities: Night 2 produced no public report of any effects before Ivan's death was announced at Day 3 night, which was out of sequence with the announced day structure. The final output listed Alice as Vanilla Villager even though Alice was attacked by the Katana on Night 1 and survived, and the Medic protection was attributed to Frank, so the protection path was unclear. Provide a running list of living players and their remaining tokens for role-holders. Clarify whether role claims are verified and whether Medic protection conflicts are resolved by the moderator. Show a consolidated vote history per day, and state how many Yakuza remain alive at each point so neutral players can plan.

The trial-ending condition (three failed nominations ending the day) was not clearly distinguished from three executions.

Night 2 deaths and role reveals were announced late, which made it hard to tell what happened when.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately ask the Sheriff or Medic for verifiable details (e.g. which target was saved) without them having to reveal publicly, and I wanted a way to privately confirm a claim with the moderator. I also wanted to see the vote history per player across the whole game in one place, since my notes got messy across several days.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Some votes were recorded as public statements that did not match the trial tallies in a clear way (e.g. Judy's Guilty vote on Erin was announced, but the tally text was hard to cross-check). The Dave death on Day 2 was announced as a Vigilante kill from a night before the Night 1 announcement sequence was clear. Ivan's death at Night 3 was announced after Carol's execution, with no Day 3 phase shown, which was confusing about whether a day had passed.
answers.suggestions: Add a compact public ledger each day listing every nomination, vote, and death with role reveals. Clarify Katana and Medic token mechanics with worked examples. Show night-action outcomes that are announced to all players, and make the Day/Night phase transitions explicit in the log so players can track the timeline without guessing.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Sheriff vs Katana when the holder dies: on N1 Dave held and used the Katana but was killed by the Vigilante, so it passed to Ivan. The rules don't say who is the 'holder at the end of the night' in this case. I ruled that Dave still counted (Not Evil), since deaths resolve in the results step. N2 raised the same question in reverse: Ivan held the Katana, was investigated by Heidi and was also killed. I applied the same ruling (Not Evil) for consistency. 2) The Fabricator has one token, but framing is free and only forging costs the token. Ivan's chat ('holding my forgery/framing token') shows players blur these, and the rules text could state it more sharply. 3) Yakuza reports are supposed to give actions but not results, yet the Katana attacker is told whether the attack succeeded. That makes it unclear how much of the outcome other Yakuza members should see. 4) The Katana vote requires majority agreement, but there is no defined procedure for when the chat counts as a vote. I treated unanimous agreement in chat as the vote.
answers.missing_information: I had no consolidated state panel. I had to track several things by hand: Katana holder, Vigilante tokens (3→2→0), Medic tokens (2→1→0), Fabricator and Clerk-style tokens, Executioner target, Jester status, and each player's current last will. The log also doesn't show the night action submissions themselves (e.g. Bob choosing Dave, Frank choosing Alice, Heidi choosing Ivan). It only shows results, which makes after-the-fact audits harder. A visit list per night would have helped me check the Lookout result (Bob and Heidi on Ivan).
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) I wanted to record the formal Katana vote (who gets the Katana, who is targeted) as a structured event rather than inferring it from chat. 2) I wanted to log my rulings, such as the Katana/Sheriff interpretation, as a visible moderator note at the moment they applied. 3) I wanted to announce the night deaths and the game-over win check as a proper Day 3 start event.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The event 'The Katana passed to Ivan' was logged mid-night, before the results step. It should resolve at the same time as Dave's death. 2) Ivan's N2 Yakuza report said 'Ivan keeps the Katana' even though Ivan died that same night. 3) Ivan's death was stamped '[Day 3 night]' instead of a Day 3 morning announcement, and no 'Day 3 begins' event or game-end announcement was logged. 4) Dave's last will ('I was a loyal villager at heart') was fine as a deception, but there's no indication whether the Fabricator could have forged it. Ivan didn't act, so it was genuine. 5) Erin (Jester) correctly lost while alive at game end. Village won once only the Jester remained alongside them, which matches the rules.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add an explicit rule: 'Katana holder at end of night' means the holder after Katana actions resolve but before death-based passing. 2) Give the moderator a state dashboard covering tokens, Katana holder, targets, last wills and per-night visit graphs. 3) Make Katana assignment and targeting a formal Yakuza vote UI. 4) Order night events strictly as actions → results → passing/transfers → private reports → day announcements. 5) Clarify which results each Yakuza member receives.

issues.description: In his Day 1 trial defense, Dave volunteered that 'night target' appeared in his private DM to Carol. Only Carol could see that DM's contents, yet he spoke as if others already knew the phrase. This publicly leaked incriminating wording, which Alice and Judy then cited as an 'admission'. Dave seemed confused about who can see private message contents.
On Day 1, Carol (the Pharmacist) privately told Dave (a Grunt with no abilities) to 'consider roleblocking Alice'. She seemed confused about which Yakuza member holds the role-block ability.

Ivan's Night 2 action is logged as his Fabricator role action ('target Heidi') when it was actually the Katana attack. This conflates the Katana with his role ability and makes it unclear whether he also framed Heidi.

After Ivan (the last Yakuza) died on Night 2, only Village players and a Jester remained, so the game should end with a Village win and a Jester loss. The log shows Ivan's death announcement but no explicit game-over announcement or declared winners.
